title: Bounded constructible derived category
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor
product is additive, let $X$ be a scheme, and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring
object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$. The *bounded constructible derived
category*
$$
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)\subseteq D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})
$$
is the full subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category
[det-def-sfb-derived-categories], the localization of all integer-indexed cochain complexes
at quasi-isomorphisms, on the
complexes $K$ that are bounded, i.e. $H^i(K)=0$ for $i$ outside a finite interval, and
all of whose cohomology sheaves $H^i(K)$ are constructible [def-sfb-constructible-module].
Morphisms are computed in $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$. No derived completeness condition is
imposed. In the specialization $\mathcal A=\Ab$, on a topologically Noetherian $X$ and for $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X$ pulled back from
[det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients-definition] one of the condensed rings $\underline E$, $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline{\Qlb}$ ($E$ a
finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$) or $\underline T$ ($T$ a finite ring killed by a
power of $\ell$), $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda_X)$ is a triangulated
subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; for a general $\mathcal R$ it need not be closed under cones. Here $\underline E$ and $\underline{\cO}_E$ use continuous functions with their $\ell$-adic topologies [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring, def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring], $\underline{\Qlb}$ uses continuous functions valued in a single finite subextension on each profinite test object [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and $\underline T$ uses the discrete topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring].

proof.text: The current convention [det-def-sfb-derived-categories] makes the ambient $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ the ordinary unbounded localization of all cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms. Only this convention is used here; the total left/right derived-functor existence hypotheses in that node are not needed to define the full subcategory. Use [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes] with exactly $\mathcal A,X,\mathcal R$ of this statement. Its ordinary unbounded ambient category, cohomological boundedness, general ring-object constructibility, ambient morphisms and absence of any completion condition give precisely the full subcategory defined here. Equivalently, [lem-sfb-bounded-constructible-iff] gives the displayed finite-interval test. This identifies the categories on objects and morphisms, with the inherited identities and composition.

source.place: First two sentences: definition and cohomological description

proof.text: Now specialize to $\mathcal A=\Ab$, $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X$ and topologically Noetherian $X$. The continuous $E$- and $\mathcal O_E$-rings, finite-subextension-valued $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-ring and discrete finite $\ell$-primary rings are exactly the alternatives of [lem-sfb-bounded-constructible-triangulated-finiteness]. For a finite ring, being killed by an $\ell$-power is equivalent to having $\ell$-power cardinality: its additive group is a finite $\ell$-group, and conversely its order kills it. That lemma makes precisely the subcategory identified in step 1 triangulated. No finite-type or characteristic assumption on $X$ is used.

source.place: Triangulatedness sentence, replacing the absent imported prop-sfb-bounded-constructible-triangulated by its existing corrected finiteness-coefficient node

proof.text: For the failure with general coefficients, fix a field $k$ and put $B=k[x,y_1,y_2,\ldots]/(xy_1,xy_2,\ldots)$ and $I=(y_1,y_2,\ldots)\subset B$. Every class has a unique expression $f(x)+g(y_1,y_2,\ldots)$ with $g$ of zero constant term. Hence $x(f+g)=xf$, so $\operatorname{ann}_B(x)=I$. This ideal is not finitely generated: for $\mathfrak m=(x,y_1,y_2,\ldots)$, the vector space $I/\mathfrak m I$ has the linearly independent basis given by all $y_i$. Finitely many ideal generators would span this quotient, a contradiction.

source.place: Final sentence: explicit scalar calculation in the noncoherent counterexample

proof.text: Take $X=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$, $\mathcal A=\Ab$ and $\mathcal R=\underline B_X$. Internal modules here are ordinary ring-sheaf modules: the sheaf action $\underline B_X\otimes F\to F$ is exactly the compatible sectionwise bilinear action, and module morphisms have the same linearity equation. By the additive exact constant realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], the cone of $x:\underline B_X[0]\to\underline B_X[0]$ has $H^{-1}=\underline I_X$ and $H^0=\underline{B/xB}_X$, with all other cohomology zero; this also follows by inserting these two degree-zero complexes in the cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The regular module is finitely presented (the cokernel of $0\to\mathcal R$), and the zero module is finitely presented, so both vertices are bounded constructible. On this one-point reduced scheme every nonempty stratum immersion is an isomorphism. Thus constructibility of $\underline I_X$ [def-sfb-constructible-module] would imply local finite presentation [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. A finite presentation [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] supplies an epimorphism from finitely many regular modules, hence local finite generation. The site has nonempty topos: the identity geometric stalk takes its initial and terminal set sheaves to the empty set and singleton. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-module-finite-type-reflection] to $I$ on this site. It would make $I$ finitely generated, contradicting step 3. Therefore the cone fails constructibility despite being bounded.

proof.text:
The subcategory is [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes]. Its description through
cohomology is [lem-sfb-bounded-constructible-iff], and for the listed coefficient rings
$\Lambda_X$ it is triangulated on a topologically Noetherian $X$ by
[prop-sfb-bounded-constructible-triangulated]. For a general $\mathcal R$, the cone of
multiplication by $x$ on the constant sheaf of
$k[x,y_1,y_2,\dots]/(xy_1,xy_2,\dots)$ on $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ is not bounded
constructible, as shown in the proof of [prop-sfb-bounded-constructible-triangulated].
